newsitem.title: USA: 2 more bodies found after U.S fireworks explosion.
newsitem.headline: 2 more bodies found after U.S fireworks explosion.

text.p: The bodies of two men were found floating in the Mississippi River Saturday, bringing to three the number of victims killed when a barge loaded with fireworks exploded during a Fourth of July celebration, police said.

Sgt. Richard Gillespie of the Alton, Ill. Police Department said the bodies of Ralph Duty, 44, and Raymond Hernandez, 24, both of Chicago, were found early on Saturday near the lock and dam at Alton, a small town near St. Louis where the celebration was held.

Fireworks were being launched from a barge on the Mississippi Thursday night when one misfired and collided with another, sparking the explosion. The body of the third man, Rick Cisneros, 45, of Markham, Ill., was found that night on the barge.

All three men were employees of The Mad Bomber pyrotechnics company of Kingsbury, Indiana. Two other employees aboard the barge, Rafael Gonzalez, 31, and Carlos Alicea, 29, survived. Gonzalez suffered a sprained ankle and Alicea was unharmed.

The Alton Fire Department said spectators were not in danger of injury from the explosion, as the barge was anchored in the middle of the river and another barge was connected to it to create a protective barrier.
